overall: Washington, DC reached a running maximum of 96.8°F by 16:52 ET, with the true daily peak confirmed at 15:04 ET — approximately 7.9 hours before the 23:00 ET observation window. Temperatures have since fallen sharply to 87.8°F by 23:00 ET, confirming a clear post-peak cooling trajectory. The day featured intense heat under mostly clear skies (cloud fraction just 12%), consistent with the Extreme Heat Warning environment in the region.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable spread among NWP models: GFS ran hot at 100.4°F while ECMWF (96.3°F) and HRRR (96.6°F) verified nearly exactly against the observed running max of 96.8°F; NBM at 97.9°F also slightly overshot. The GFS appears to be an outlier, and the observed peak already in hand makes the NWP spread largely moot — the models that verified best (ECMWF, HRRR) were tightly clustered around today's actual observed high.
max_temp_prediction: With the daily peak locked in at 96.8°F as of 16:52 ET and temperatures now 9°F below that level at 23:00 ET, today's TMAX is virtually certain to be 96.8°F — firmly within the 96-97°F even bucket. The META model's 57.5% weight on the 98-99°F bucket and D1_NOW's 33.0% on the same appear to be pre-peak model artifacts that did not fully account for the observed peak timing; the intraday observational evidence overwhelmingly favors the 96-97°F bucket. Confidence is very high given the peak is confirmed 7.9 hours in the past with clear overnight cooling underway.
